tagline: The inland road through the Black's Woods, ghost included.
intro: Out of Franklin, Route 182 turns east into unorganized territory on the old Black's Woods Road and winds among lakes and mountains, past Fox Pond, Spring River Lake and Tunk Lake and under Tunk and Catherine mountains, before coming down into Cherryfield by the Narraguagus River. US 1 keeps to the coast to the south. This road keeps to the woods.
Franklin, where it starts, has lived on ship masts, railroad ties, granite, blueberries and Christmas trees, in that order.

moments.title: Catherine's Hill
moments.text: Where the road tops out near Catherine Mountain, travelers tell of a woman in a light blue gown asking for a ride, sometimes to Bar Harbor, and of trouble for those who refuse.

moments.title: Narraguagus River
moments.text: Anglers once came from afar for the Memorial Day weekend opening of the Atlantic salmon fly fishing here, a run much reduced since.

moments.title: Cherryfield
moments.text: Named for the wild cherries that once grew along the river, the self-styled Blueberry Capital keeps a 75-acre historic district on both banks, with buildings from about 1750 to 1890.
